value.rationale: The smallest prime coprime to the six-phase alphabet is five, and five is the first length at which a sixth-root zero sum can arise as 2+3. This creates a natural first composite-alphabet regime beyond the 0/4-row trichotomy. The theorem gives a sharp nontrivial cross-STFT support threshold 19 rather than 5, a complete attainable-support gap (6–18 missing), all eight row-zero configurations with exact design counts, and structural descriptions of the two exceptional classes. These are concrete phase-code null-pattern and recoverability constraints, not arbitrary slices or mere numerical simulations.
